title: Calling All Cars
paragraphs: Early police procedural/true-crime dramatization based on Los Angeles-area law-enforcement cases. Frozen GRH snapshot has 296 dated recordings from Dec. 6, 1933 through Sept. 8, 1939.
GRH documents the program through CBS West Coast police-drama run (November 29, 1933 to September 8, 1939) on [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Charles Frederick Lindsley (narrator on 210 recordings, announcer on 1 recording, and host on 1 recording), Jesse Rosenquist (performer on 131 recordings and narrator on 1 recording), James E. Davis (host on 44 recordings and performer on 18 recordings), William N. Robson (producer on 38 recordings, writer on 37 recordings, radio adaptor on 3 recordings, performer on 2 recordings, and director on 1 recording), [[person|gale-gordon|Gale Gordon]] (narrator on 17 recordings, host on 16 recordings, and performer on 3 recordings), Eugene Viskerloos (host on 7 recordings and performer on 4 recordings), and Frederick Stark (conductor on 10 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.5d1a575385a05456|CBS Pacific Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.50630574777d6937|Don Lee Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, police investigation, robbery and burglary, kidnapping and missing persons, forensic evidence and ballistics, and narcotics and illegal drugs.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Depression-era urban crime and public safety, Police-public relations through network radio, and Early popularization of forensic police methods.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (21 shared credited people), [[show|suspense|Suspense]] (10 shared credited people), [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]] (8 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (9 shared credited people), and [[show|the-great-gildersleeve|The Great Gildersleeve]] (9 shared credited people).
